uncertainties: This is a 121-lemma sample out of 1098 per language. It is not a complete glossary review, and other lemmas may contain errors.
No native-speaker review was performed. Every 'requires-native-review' item, and the suggested wordings in confirmed items, need native validation before publication.
Each lemma comes with one context sentence only. Glosses were judged against the Turkish reference and that sentence, and other senses in other stories were not assessed.
bloom: the context uses the noun ('in bloom'), while the Turkish reference and all glosses are verbs. This is a reference-level choice, not a per-language error.
tear: the context shows 'tore'. The 'rip' sense is covered in all languages, but it is unclear whether the 'teardrop' sense is needed for this story.

wardrobe: the Turkish reference 'gardırop' may itself be read as furniture only. The wardrobe findings are most likely a source-reference issue that propagated to all languages; pt-BR 'guarda-roupa' covers both senses.
hedge: hi/ur/bn give a generic 'fence', matching the generic Turkish 'çit'. This is acceptable, but a 'living hedge' nuance is lost; not flagged.

Minor part-of-speech mismatches were not flagged as errors. Examples: ru 'быстрый' for adverbial 'runs fast', ru 'правильный' for 'they were right' (predicative 'правы'), and hi 'खतरे में डालने वाला' (adjectival) for the gerund 'without endangering'.
Arabic vowel-less forms (e.g. 'معرّض') are ambiguous. Whether the app displays diacritics affects the severity of that finding.
summary: I checked all 1210 lemma-language pairs (121 lemmas × 10 languages) and flagged 37 findings: 1 high, 22 medium and 14 low. Recurring issues: 'confusion' glossed as mental bewilderment instead of commotion (6 languages); 'wardrobe' glossed only as furniture when the context means a clothes collection (8 languages, likely inherited from the reference); and 'find' glossed as 'search' in hi and ur. Other notable cases are 'have' as 'keep/place' (hi, ur), 'short' as 'brief' (ur), 'remained' as 'stayed' (vi), and an ambiguous passive reading of Arabic 'endangering'. Most other glosses look acceptable for their context. Findings marked 'requires-native-review' need native confirmation, and this sample does not establish that the full glossary is correct.
